Modern GPU drivers can't do nearest neighbor upscaling

Displaying a 1080p input on a 4k screen results in a blurry, filtered mess. Would it kill them to use nearest neighbor instead of bilinear/bicubic when the input and output resolutions are exact integer multiples?

nVidia and AMD been ignoring this for years now.

Are you sure that isn't your display doing the scaling? I wouldn't really know. Last time I played something that didn't allow the native resolution of my display I went into the geforce drivers and made it add letterboxing to prevent anything from scaling.

Note: I'm not actually experiencing this problem now as I use a different monitor for gaming, but it's holding me back from upgrading my display (ideally, I'd like to be future-proof for 4k while also being able to play at 1080p or letterboxed 1440p).

Generally speaking, monitors don't do any scaling and rely on the OS/GPU to provide a scaled image, while TVs have built-in upscalers. A few 4k TVs have the option to do integer scaling but most of them don't and force the image through a crappy upscale filter. So in my case, it's certainly because of the GPU driver.

Windows actually has a pixel-perfect scaling implementation, so you can actually get a 1080p game to fill up a 4k screen without any filtering if you can get it to run in borderless windowed mode and scale it via Windows settings, but it's a bit messy to get this working and is not without issues.
